title: GET /api/dashboard/metrics returns risk/vendor/audit-assurance KPI data with no per-module permission check
description: dashboard-metrics/index.js's router only calls router.use(authenticate) — none of /metrics, /risk-distribution, /risk-areas, or /:orgId ever call requirePermission or requireAllPermissions. This is a materially looser gate than the drill-down boards under /api/client/dashboard/executive/*, which each require requireAllPermissions(['compliance.read', '<module>.read']) (executive-dashboard.routes.js boardPermission()). A caller holding only compliance.read (no risk.read/vendor.read/audit.read/scan.read) can still see aggregated risk/vendor/audit KPI numbers on the main dashboard cards even though the matching drill-down board would reject them. Verify whether this is the intended design or a real enforcement gap between the summary cards and their own drill-downs.
preconditions: User with a role holding compliance.read only — no risk.read, vendor.read, audit.read, framework.read, or scan.read
steps: As the same user, call GET /api/client/dashboard/executive/risk-summary
expectedResult: If module-level KPI visibility is meant to mirror the drill-down boards' permission model, data.risk/data.vendorRisk/data.audit should be withheld or empty in the first call; the second call correctly 403s today. Flag any mismatch found for triage rather than assuming either behavior is correct.

title: A non-admin cannot pull another project's data into /api/dashboard/metrics via ?projectIds=
description: resolveProjectIdsScope silently drops any requested project ID that isn't in the caller's own ProjectMember set for a non-admin (unlike resolveProjectScope, which throws 403 on a single foreign ID). Verify the drop actually happens rather than the foreign ID leaking into the $in match.
preconditions: User is a member of Project A only; Project B belongs to the same org but the user has no ProjectMember row for it
expectedResult: The response's numbers reflect Project A only; Project B's risks/vendors/findings never appear, and no error is thrown for the foreign ID.

title: GET /api/dashboard/:orgId rejects a path orgId belonging to a different organization
description: The :orgId handler compares requestedOrgId against req.orgId and req.permissions.has('organization.admin') before calling fetchProviderCoverage. A caller without organization.admin who supplies any orgId other than their own must be rejected before any query runs.
preconditions: Two distinct orgs A and B; caller belongs to org A only, no organization.admin
steps: As the org A caller, call GET /api/dashboard/<org B's ObjectId>
expectedResult: 403 Access denied, with no providerCoverage data for org B in the response body.

title: Two non-admin users with disjoint project memberships never receive each other's cached dashboard response
description: resolveProjectIdsScope's output feeds scopeCacheKey, which must produce distinct cache keys for distinct resolved project-ID sets. Guards against the previously-fixed bug where naively stringifying the {$in:[...]} array collapsed to '[object Object]' for every non-admin, letting any two non-admins in the same org share one Redis-cached response regardless of their actual project access.
preconditions: User X is a member of Project A only; User Y is a member of Project B only; both in the same org
steps: As User X, call GET /api/dashboard/metrics (no projectIds override) and record the response
Immediately after, as User Y, call GET /api/dashboard/metrics (no projectIds override)
expectedResult: User Y's response reflects Project B's data, not User X's cached Project A response.

title: A malformed projectIds value is rejected with 400, not silently swallowed into a Mongo query
description: resolveProjectIdsScope validates every comma-separated entry with mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid before use, throwing AppError.badRequest('Invalid projectId in projectIds') on the first bad entry.
steps: Call GET /api/client/dashboard/executive/risk-summary?projectIds=<24 zero chars>,'; return true;//
expectedResult: Both calls return 400 with a validation error; neither reaches the aggregation pipeline with the malformed value.

title: requireAllPermissions on a board endpoint truly requires both permissions, not either
description: boardPermission('risk') = requireAllPermissions(['compliance.read', 'risk.read']). A caller with only one of the two permissions must still be rejected — verifies this isn't accidentally implemented as an OR check.
preconditions: User A holds compliance.read but not risk.read
User B holds risk.read but not compliance.read
steps: As User B, call the same endpoint
expectedResult: Both calls return 403 — only a caller holding both compliance.read AND risk.read succeeds.
